_comment: Build Log — living per-project documentation. Edit as each project is built; the panel (panels/build_log.html) re-renders from this file. Schema per project: id, name, week, status(done|in_progress|planned|slipped), headline, metrics[{label,value}], entries[{date,title,status,detail,refs[{label,kind(commit|file|run|link),href}]}], decisions[{title,detail}]. Newest entries first.

projects.name: Music Genre — BEARDOWN
projects.headline: Genre family mk1→mk2→mk2.5→mk3 complete. mk3 (3-sec clips, ×10 rows) lands voted-to-track 0.807 — +4.7 over mk2 (apples-to-apples). The mk2.5 finding REPRODUCED at scale: every reliability axis is flat as a test-rank predictor (U −0.10, RRM_w +0.10), accuracy (+0.43) the only signal. Effective-N ≈1.4× (ICC 0.68) predicted the dead U before the run; batch_refit confirmed it. FORGE multi-model integration next.

metrics.label: mk3 data
metrics.value: 3-sec fused3 · 9,990 seg → 6,992/1,498/1,500 · same tracks as mk1/mk2

entries.title: mk3 metric validation (×10 data) — RRM & U still flat: mk2.5 reproduced
entries.detail: Firewalled study on the 3-sec sweep: refit all 20 configs on full-train, recorded TEST (selection stayed CV-only). Spearman rank-agreement with TEST accuracy — CV accuracy +0.429 (the only predictor, though weaker than mk2.5's +0.685 as more correlated rows noise-up every CV estimate), RRM +0.139, fold-stability −s +0.130, RRM_w +0.099, epistemic −U −0.095. Ten times the rows did NOT revive the epistemic axis. Mechanism, predicted BEFORE the run: within-track segment correlation (ICC 0.681) gives a design-effect 7.12, so 6,992 segments are worth ≈982 independent-equivalent — the last-layer σ tightens by only √(982/700)≈18%, inside the noise. The central negative result now holds on a SECOND dataset at an order of magnitude more rows. Three configs tie for best TEST 0.789 (incl. cfg 17, the accuracy-best RRM buried at 16/20).

entries.title: mk3 voted-to-track 0.807 — +4.7 over mk2 (apples-to-apples)
entries.detail: The sweep reports PER-SEGMENT accuracy (one row per 3-sec clip); mk1/mk2 reported PER-TRACK. Not comparable. vote_eval collapses a track's ~10 segment predictions by prob-sum majority → one prediction per song. Deployed cfg 19: per-segment 0.789 / macro-F1 0.788 → voted-to-track 0.807 / macro-F1 0.807, vote gain +0.018 (the denoising of ambiguous clips). Per-track 0.807 vs mk2's 0.760 = +4.7. macro-F1 ≈ accuracy → no genre sacrificed; classical 1.00, pop/country/rock 0.667 = the stable GTZAN confusion cluster (same genres that capped mk2). The +4.7 is real but bounded — exactly the ≈1.4× effective-N story, not the ×10 the row count suggests.

entries.title: mk3 RRM sweep — 20-config reliability sweep on 3-sec fused3 (GPU)
entries.detail: Same engine, search space, and selection as the mk2 sweep — only the DATA changed (controlled experiment: data density is the single variable). 20 configs, 3-fold GroupKFold-by-track. RRM winner = cfg 19 (A 0.778); accuracy-best = cfg 17 (A 0.800 — the mk2 deployed architecture, img768/tab256/concat). r(A,RRM) = −0.067: RRM again uncorrelated with accuracy, driven −0.88 by the fold-instability penalty s, and it buried the accuracy-best cfg 17 at rank 16/20. Deployed cfg 19 refit → VAL 0.776 / TEST 0.789 (per-segment), acceptance PASS (val≥0.75), φ-dim 384.

entries.title: GPU switch — CPU→CUDA, one-line torch reinstall (simple + worthwhile)
entries.detail: The 3-sec sweep (6,992 train segments × 3 folds × 20 configs) was crawling on CPU — minutes per config. The RTX 4070 SUPER (12 GB) was present, but the installed torch was a CPU-only build (torch.cuda.is_available() → False). One-line fix: pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124 → torch 2.6.0+cu124, CUDA visible (the driver's CUDA 13.2 is the max it supports, not what you install — a cu124 wheel runs forward-compatibly). No code change: train.py / sweep.py / batch_refit.py were already --device-flagged. Result: full-train refit 36 s (from a multi-minute CPU crawl); full 20-config sweep ≈26 min; batch_refit ≈10 min. The cheapest high-leverage move of the week — the canonical 'do this first on any torch box' note.

entries.title: mk3 data path — leakage-safe 3-sec fused3, verified torch-free
entries.detail: New _load_fused3: each 3-sec tabular segment is joined MANY-TO-ONE to its parent track's single mel spectrogram (no spectrogram cutting — the image is track-level). Split is on TRACK ids via stratified seed 42, the SAME partition as mk1/mk2, so segments inherit their parent's split and data density is the only variable. 9,990 segments → 6,992/1,498/1,500. The existing 30-sec _load_fused is byte-untouched (mk1/mk2 numbers can't move); fused3 is dual-input like fused, so LLLA/HMC/bundle attach unchanged. verify_mk3 (7 checks) + sanity_check confirm: dual-input contract, many-to-one join (9.99 seg/track share one image), 0 tracks straddle (a naive segment split would leak 97.1% of tracks — Sturm 2013), scaler fit on train segments only, 57 named axes intact. All pure-numpy — ran and passed BEFORE any GPU time.

entries.title: Input-feature attribution wired — bundle self-describes (rung 2)
entries.detail: attribution.py: the LLLA epistemic scale v(φ;τ) pushed back onto NAMED inputs. Closed form dv/dφ = 2(H+τI)⁻¹φ (verified vs finite-difference to 1.6e-9), chained with ONE backbone vector-Jacobian product → per-feature epistemic sensitivity dv/dx; τ factors out, so a cached M lets FORGE recompute live for any τ (identity verified exact across τ). write_bundle now emits inputs.json (the 57 named axes) + bundle.json (a capabilities list that gates the FORGE attribution tab). 6/6 torch-free tests pass. This names what INFO 510 Table A3 could only rank anonymously. The torch precompute (dφ/dx) runs once on the GPU box; FORGE then serves static numpy — the ggn_eig.npz pattern.

entries.title: mk2.5 metric validation — RRM falsified, honestly (the finding)
entries.detail: Firewalled study: refit all 20 configs on full-train, recorded test (selection stayed CV-only). Spearman rank-agreement with TEST accuracy — CV accuracy +0.685, but RRM_w −0.002, equal-weight RRM −0.022, fold-stability −0.008, epistemic U −0.028: every reliability axis is noise as a test-rank predictor. Mechanism: post-hoc LLLA on a frozen DET head gives a near-constant U (0.0258–0.0343), and s is test-uncorrelated. A precise negative result — refines, not refutes, INFO 510 (their RRM used TRAINED Bayesian heads where U varied). Boundary condition: RRM earns its keep only when the reliability axes are both variable AND test-predictive.

entries.title: mk2.5 — Dirichlet / variance re-selection lens (no new model)
entries.detail: Generalized RRM to a simplex weighting: RRM_w = 1−√(Σ wᵢ vᵢ²), w∈Δ²; the locked equal-weight metric is the centroid. Variance-derived w=(0.008,0.926,0.067) zeroes the uninformative U axis on principle → selects cfg 17. Dirichlet sweep (200k uniform-simplex draws): cfg 17 49.5%, cfg 12 48.2%, rest <2% — two robust contenders, choice is weighting-dependent (the only region favoring cfg 12 weights the flat U axis). A selection LENS over sweep.json — no model, no bundle, no FORGE/attribution impact.

entries.title: mk2 locked = cfg 17 — first acceptance PASS, beats mk1 +6 test
entries.detail: Deployed the variance-weighted RRM_w winner: cfg 17 (img768 / tab256 / concat / adam / lr 2.4e-4 / do 0.21,0.17 / ep75, φ-dim 768). Refit on full-train → VAL 0.793 / TEST 0.760 / test macro-F1 0.760, first acceptance PASS (val≥0.75) and clears the paper's 0.766 val band. The macro-F1 jump (0.686→0.760) is on the WEAK genres — a better-balanced classifier, not a luckier one. Equal-weight RRM's nominal winner was cfg 12 (kept as documented contrast); cfg 12 wins ONLY on the flat U axis, so it loses once U is correctly down-weighted. Round-trip OK, max|Δ|=0 — FORGE wraps it unchanged.

entries.title: mk2 sweep — 20-config RRM-selected reliability sweep
entries.detail: Built sweep.py (reuses train.py + llla.py): 20 configs × 3-fold GroupKFold-by-track, each scored on a 4-axis catalogue (accuracy A, fold-σ s, LLLA epistemic U at shared-α τ, off-diagonal rate) + RAM / Pareto / Pearson / dCor. The Bayesian layer is post-hoc LLLA over the frozen det head — the SAME object FORGE serves (selection-U == display-U). Ran clean on CPU (~54 min); catalogue persisted to sweep.json.

entries.title: Input-feature attribution — specced + verified-amenable
entries.detail: Locked the design (FORGE_input_feature_attribution_SPEC.txt): push LLLA σ back through the frozen backbone, ∂σ/∂x = (∂σ/∂φ)·(∂φ/∂x), to NAME which input feature drives a prediction's epistemic uncertainty — the latent features INFO 510 Table A3 could only rank anonymously. Verified against the live bundle: scaler.json carries all 57 named axes + mean/std, arch.json+weights.pt rebuild the frozen backbone — so attribution runs on mk1, cfg 17 and future mk3 with ZERO re-bundling. Ships via precompute-and-cache (mirrors ggn_eig), tabular branch first.

entries.title: Bayesian layer live — LLLA over the frozen head
entries.detail: Last-layer Laplace (closed form from the cached GGN eigenbasis) over the frozen det head: the 0.714 point estimate becomes a decomposable posterior with a live τ-knob. This is the object mk2's RRM selects on AND the object FORGE displays — one llla.py call, two consumers.

entries.title: ML usage / cost estimator built
entries.detail: _shared/usage.py turns every compute.json into energy / carbon / $ with measured-vs-modeled tags, an actual-power hook (RAPL / nvidia-smi), a suite roll-up, and a pre-run projection. Assumptions live in an override YAML for real rates IRL.

entries.title: Song drop-in inference verified (wav + mp3)
entries.detail: End-to-end: drop audio → 30-s windows → clean mel + 57 features → per-genre scores with MC-dropout σ. load_audio hardened (soundfile → librosa fallback → clear error, no silent skip). Works because train + inference now share one mel recipe (validate r=1.0).

entries.title: Backbone frozen: clean-128 / batch-8, CV 0.714
entries.detail: Batch 32→8 lifted CV 0.629→0.714 (+0.086). The frozen deterministic backbone the Bayesian head attaches to. 6× cheaper to train than the original 224 dirty pipeline and the only variant that does real-audio drop-in correctly.

entries.title: Gap diagnosis complete — every cheap hypothesis ruled out
entries.detail: Early stopping, epochs, representation, split, and resolution all tested and eliminated as the cause of the 0.07 gap to 0.766. Lever was batch size; residual is framework (Keras vs PyTorch) + run variance. Faithful, documented reproduction.

entries.title: Clean log-mel regeneration (silent-failure fix)
entries.detail: Kaggle grey PNGs are colormapped matplotlib figures — luminance non-monotonic in mel energy, so a dropped song scored noise. Regenerated all spectrograms from audio with one recipe → train + inference share extract_mel → validate passes by construction.

entries.title: Architecture vetted against the public INFO_510 repo
entries.detail: Confirmed cfg_14: 57 features (length dropped), gated fusion, deterministic head, dense 512/192, lr 7.37e-5, adam, 75 epochs. The winning head was already det — so the FORGE det-backbone + LLLA reproduction is bit-faithful with zero mechanism mismatch.

decisions.title: mk2 = cfg 17, selected by variance-weighted RRM_w (CV-only)
decisions.detail: Deploy the accuracy-strong + stable config; the only metric-region favoring the equal-weight winner (cfg 12) weights the flat, test-uncorrelated U axis. Selection never saw test (firewall).

decisions.title: RRM falsified honestly — the negative result IS the contribution
decisions.detail: On a frozen-det head, neither reliability axis predicts test rank (RRM_w ρ=−0.00, accuracy ρ=+0.69). Built the apparatus to falsify our own metric, ran it, reported it. Refines INFO 510's boundary, doesn't refute it.

decisions.title: Keep BOTH bundles as the result
decisions.detail: beardown_rrm (=cfg 17, deployed) and beardown_rrm_cfg12 (=equal-weight winner). The comparison between them is the mk2.5 finding.

decisions.title: mk3 = beardown_3sec, motivated not guessed
decisions.detail: mk2.5's mechanism (flat U) hands mk3 a hypothesis: does ×10 data (3-sec clips) make U vary again and revive RRM_w's validity? Needs a leakage-safe cutter (track-grouped split).

decisions.title: Batch size was the lever (+0.086 CV)
decisions.detail: 32→8 lifted CV 0.629→0.714. Smaller batch = gradient-noise regularization on small data. Batch 8 is also the BatchNorm floor for this net and matches cfg_14.

decisions.title: 224 resolution ruled out
decisions.detail: Dirty-224 scored CV 0.629 — erased the batch-8 gain at 6× the compute and 3× the memory. Resolution is not the lever.

decisions.title: Clean log-mel over dirty Kaggle grey
decisions.detail: Clean mels score ≥ dirty AND are the only representation reproducible at inference from a dropped wav. A deliberate, documented improvement over the original pipeline.

decisions.title: Split is not the gap
decisions.detail: BEARDOWN's seed-42 stratified split scored ≈ our track split (0.673 vs 0.70) — ruling out an unlucky-draw explanation for the gap.

decisions.title: Freeze, don't chase 0.766
decisions.detail: The wall at ~0.71 is precisely FORGE's motivating example: accuracy-only selection stalls and says nothing about trust. The Bayesian layer is the answer, not more tuning.

decisions.title: mk3 = 3-sec tab ⨝ 30-sec image (many-to-one), not a re-render
decisions.detail: A true per-segment 3-sec image would need re-rendering from the wavs. The effective-N analysis showed it isn't worth it for the U-question: the last-layer posterior conditions on φ, which already diversifies ≈10× through the tabular half under many-to-one, while within-track image correlation caps the marginal gain of distinct 3-sec images at ≈2–3×. Many-to-one runs today with zero re-render and is the cfg-17 architecture on 10× rows — the controlled data-density test.

decisions.title: GPU was the iteration lever (simple + worthwhile)
decisions.detail: One-line cu124 torch reinstall took the sweep from a CPU crawl to 36 s/refit. No code change — the pipeline was already device-flagged. Recorded as the canonical first move on any torch box; the driver's max-CUDA number is not the wheel you install.

decisions.title: Deployed cfg 19 (RRM winner); cfg 17 is the accuracy-best contender
decisions.detail: The sweep auto-deployed its RRM winner, cfg 19 (voted-to-track 0.807). But cfg 17 is accuracy-best (A 0.800) and TIES for best held-out TEST (0.789) — and it is the config RRM buried at 16/20. Recommendation on the record: promote cfg 17 as the mk3 headline and keep cfg 19 as the labeled RRM-winner contrast, mirroring mk2's cfg17-vs-cfg12 pairing so the selection pathology is visible in FORGE. (cfg 17 promote pending.)

decisions.title: U did not revive at ×10 data — predicted, then measured
decisions.detail: Effective-N ≈1.4× (ICC 0.681) predicted the last-layer σ would tighten only ~18%, too little to move the epistemic axis; batch_refit confirmed −U Spearman −0.095. The mk2.5 boundary condition holds at scale: reliability axes need a TRAINED Bayesian head (INFO 510), not post-hoc LLLA on a frozen DET head. This refines, does not refute, the source paper — now on two datasets.

projects.name: Phonon DOS
projects.headline: Phonon DOS (51-bin regression, Chen et al. 2021 E(3)-equivariant reproduction) wrapped by the full FORGE posterior observatory — the genre template applied to a regression head and driven to a working full-stack dashboard. LLLA manufactures a last-layer posterior over every frozen backbone (mk1 e3nn_repro / mk2 EMD / mk3 js), the τ-knob + HMC gold-standard run live in-browser + server-side, and the verdict is now a continuous data-limited confidence (γ = λ/(λ+τ)) rather than a binary. Real ATLAS model work proceeds in parallel (W6).

entries.title: HMC made full-stack + the visualization that gives the Gaussians meaning
entries.detail: Wired the FIRE HMC VALIDATION button to a real server-side sampler (Flask GET /api/forge/hmc → forge.hmc_run), with a synthetic-bundle fallback so the full-stack path runs out of the box before real bundles exist. hmc_run projects the sampled last-layer weights onto a probe crystal to give the predicted DOS intensity at a frequency — a readable scalar — and returns the chain trace + sample histogram + the analytic Laplace N(mean,σ) for the same quantity. The UI fires → shows a sampling/progress animation → renders per-bin cards: chain-trace plot (draw-in) + histogram with the Laplace Gaussian overlaid. That overlay is the point: it turns the abstract weight-Gaussians into 'does our fast approximation match the gold standard?' — verdict GOOD when they line up. This is the ATLAS HMC-check pattern reused.

entries.title: Last-Layer Model panel — the head as W-map + full posterior, with a click-to-inspect Gaussian
entries.detail: A concrete model of the exact object LLLA Bayes-ifies: the linear head W(32→51) as a heatmap (MEAN), a σ-heatmap (UNCERTAINTY), and an ALL-POSTERIORS bell grid drawing every one of the 1,632 weights as its N(mean,σ). Click any cell → a large, real prior N(0,σ₀) vs posterior N(mean,σ) overlay (σ₀=√(σ²_k/τ), σ=√(σ²_k·featⱼ)), so you watch the data pull a weight off the prior. Carries the honest caveat on-panel: LLLA models ONLY the last layer (backbone φ frozen), so a Deep Ensemble / subnetwork Laplace is what would add feature uncertainty. All τ-reactive, recomputed in-browser from the shipped eigenbasis (U, λ, σ²).

entries.title: Continuous verdict — data-limited as a confidence %, not a yes/no
entries.detail: Replaced the binary DATA-LIMITED / CAPACITY-LIMITED headline with a graded readout. Each eigen-direction's data-information fraction γ = λ/(λ+τ) ∈ [0,1] is the continuous version of the old λ>τ cut; the verdict % = 1 − eff_dim/d (mean prior-mass). Shown as a spectrum bar with a marker plus four %-confidence gauges — capacity utilization (eff_dim/d), posterior fidelity (Laplace-vs-HMC), epistemic saturation (data-frac), calibration (PICP vs 95%). The eigenspectrum now colours by γ (amber prior → cyan data) instead of a hard two-colour split. All derived from quantities already in the payload, so it works in every data tier.

entries.title: Optimization Frontier + independent calculation CLI
entries.detail: Optimization Frontier panel: a model×RRM-component heat map (1−A, s, U, ‖v‖; brighter = more room) plus a Pareto front in accuracy-gap vs uncertainty space with dominated backbones arrowed toward the frontier — 'where is the room to improve'. Fed by a compact forge_roster.json. Independent CLI forge_cli.py computes every metric from scratch and tweakably: synth · fit · posterior · metrics · hmc · datafrac · attribution · predict · payload · verify · roster (each takes --tau, --json). synth→fit→payload regenerates the whole dashboard payload with zero server, so nothing on the dashboard is hard-coded — the static tier is CLI output.

entries.title: Posterior observatory dashboard stood up (τ grab-slider, live recompute, 3-tier source)
entries.detail: The phonon FORGE dashboard (forge.html + Flask server.py + forge_dashboard.py payload assembler): 3-column TRON observatory wrapping ANY frozen backbone with an LLLA head. τ is a grab-slider that live-recomputes the eigen-split AND the LLLA predictive band in-browser (closed form off the shipped c=Uᵀz, σ²); big animated buttons; a calc scan-line/pulse animation; 80vw layout. Data loads in three source-badged tiers: ● LIVE (/api/forge/dashboard recomputes at τ) → ● COMPUTED (CLI-generated static payload) → ● DEMO SEED. mk1/mk2/mk3 are all treated as frozen backbones FORGE wraps — mk1 (deterministic) included, since manufacturing a posterior for a point-estimate model is the whole point of FORGE.

entries.title: LLLA head + intercept fix for the DOS regression
entries.detail: llla.py fit for the phonon regression head (fit_bundle → W, U, λ, σ², μ, sd, ymean). Key fix: a phonon DOS spectrum has a nonzero baseline the zero-intercept head couldn't represent, which showed up as a catastrophic R² (≈ −27); adding a Y-centering intercept (ymean, backward-compatible on load) lifted it to R² ≈ 0.95 with PICP ≈ 0.95 on the template bundle. This is the same closed-form last-layer object as genre — one llla.py, wrapped by the observatory and the HMC validator alike.

entries.title: Apply the standalone build template
entries.detail: EDA → experimental design → model-lock → LLLA + HMC → local dashboard → compute metrics, mirroring the genre build.

decisions.title: FORGE wraps every backbone — including deterministic mk1
decisions.detail: mk1 (e3nn_repro, pure MSE, no built-in uncertainty) is not the thing FORGE can't handle; it's the raw material. LLLA manufactures a last-layer posterior for it exactly as for mk2/mk3. Each backbone yields a different φ geometry → a genuinely different epistemic read, so the registry is a real uncertainty-method comparison.

decisions.title: Read nonclosure from the DNCQN plateau, not TEC eval-closure (carried into phonon's verdict framing)
decisions.detail: The graded data-limited confidence mirrors the ABCD finding: the honest systematic is read from where the gradient self-terminates (the prior-led plateau), not from pushing through the noise floor.

decisions.title: Verdict is continuous, not binary
decisions.detail: A hard λ>τ cut throws away the graded γ = λ/(λ+τ) information. The dashboard now reports a %-confidence and per-direction γ, which is both more honest and reads better.

decisions.title: HMC validates the Gaussian everything else rides on
decisions.detail: Every uncertainty shown elsewhere is the fast Laplace approximation. The full-stack HMC run samples the true posterior and overlays it — the single check that licenses trusting all the cheap Gaussians. Synthetic fallback keeps it runnable before real bundles exist.
